title: Manual tri-star hand truck for one courier with 60 kg parcel v2
problem_restatement: Carry a 60 kg parcel up and down domestic stairs with one courier and fold to a suitcase for van stow with auto-locked holding.
mechanism_sentence: A 60 kg parcel rides on a folding plate held to a braced two-tube frame that rolls on paired wheels on flat floors and pivots over 197 mm steps on three-wheel clusters that stay locked until the handle levers are squeezed.
decisive_choices: Twin-tube backbone with clip-on brace (C22+C28) because it carries 88.3 N m at 51.1 MPa with 13.8 mm braced deflection versus 0.11 m whip while keeping backbone one piece where hinges would cut stiffness.
Tri-star cluster (C1) because it pivots over the 197 mm riser with 185 mm radius at 39.0 N m per side costing 116 J per riser where posture or handle notes alone do no stepping.
Dead-man lever with disc plus tooth park pin (C7+C20) because release means locked holding 67.0 N m against 209 N pull and 188 N hold where friction-only contact alone cannot be trusted.
open_question: Can one tired hand reliably release, meter and re-lock the lever and tooth engagement on a 197 mm riser in a built-hardware bench test?
transfer_line: Load: folding toe-plate -> twin-tube backbone -> tri-star cluster | Measured: hand lever -> disc caliper

assumed_constraints.constraint: design step envelope maximum riser height 197 mm and minimum tread depth 254 mm per International Residential Code
stowed envelope must fit smallest urban van door 1120 mm wide x 1235 mm high and floor 1802x1535 mm with 1253 mm height

concept.working_principle: Parcel to folding toe-plate to one-piece twin-tube backbone with clip-on brace to main axle to two tri-star clusters to step, and grips to cable to disc caliper plus tooth park pin to cluster plate; pulling backward uphill pivots on stopped lead wheel, lowering forward downhill reverses it, with no free back-drive when lever released.

fabrication_steps.description: Make the twin-tube L-frame backbone first, because toe-plate, axle, handle and brace all fix to it
Fit the main axle and two tri-star clusters with discs next, because brake torque must align to the backbone
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted steel axle 20 mm dia, 150 mm solid-rubber wheels, 160 mm rotor

fabrication_steps.description: Pin the folding toe-plate and telescoping handle plus clip-on brace next, because they restore the load path when deployed
fabrication_steps.method: Pinned aluminium toe-plate 365 x 240 mm, 8 mm pin, telescoping steel handle

fabrication_steps.description: Route the dead-man cable with slack loop and set caliper and tooth pin last, because fold must never tension the brake
fabrication_steps.method: Cabled steel lever with 160 mm caliper and tooth park pin

risks.risk: Lever needs too much finger force or tooth fails to engage on stairs.
risks.mitigation: Bench test lever release and tooth engagement with one tired hand on built hardware.

risks.risk: Folding tensions brake cable and releases lock.
risks.mitigation: Run cable with slack loop at sliding handle and allow fold only when brake locked.

risks.risk: Repeated stair impact overloads frame or lets axle wander off step nose.
risks.mitigation: Keep one-piece backbone with clip-on brace for 13.8 mm stiffness and 3.60 factor with impact.

novelty_claim: One-piece twin-tube backbone with clip-on transverse brace plus spring-applied disc with tooth park lock on tri-star axle with fold interlock.
